This paper examines the expressive power of constraints in Constraint Handling Rules (CHR), a declarative, constraint-oriented rewriting system. We demonstrate that the leading atom within a rule's head determines the rule's expressiveness; specifically, a head containing $n$ atoms is strictly more powerful than one with $n-1$ atoms. Furthermore, we establish that a CHR program capable of executing $n$ unifications can be fully simulated by another program that employs only heads requiring at most $n$ atoms in their definitions.

This study investigates the alignment of galaxy spin axes with the dipole of the galaxy spin direction distribution. Utilizing data from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) and the 2dF Galaxy Redshift Survey (2dFGRS), we examine spin directions for galaxies within the redshift range $0.1 < z < 0.4$. Our analysis reveals that the dipole axes for the spin direction distribution are consistent with those derived from the luminosity distribution in both surveys. Furthermore, we observe that the galaxy spin directions are not randomly distributed relative to these dipole axes. While the spin directions of galaxies in the $0.1 < z < 0.2$ bin show no significant preference for alignment with the dipole, those in the $0.2 < z < 0.4$ bin exhibit a clear tendency to align. These findings corroborate earlier research indicating that the galaxy spin direction distribution is not isotropic.

Few-shot learning (FSL) has emerged as a critical area of research, driven by the need for rapid adaptation to new tasks with minimal data. While existing FSL approaches typically rely on sampling from a dataset's feature space, this strategy is vulnerable to label noise and dataset bias. To address these limitations, we introduce Eigen-Reptile, a method that integrates the Eigen-Covariance metric with Reptile optimization. Unlike traditional methods, Eigen-Reptile explicitly models the feature space to mitigate biases and enhance robustness against noisy labels. Furthermore, the approach employs a meta-learning framework to learn task-specific representations, enabling efficient generalization across diverse few-shot scenarios. Empirical results on the few-shot classification benchmark demonstrate that Eigen-Reptile outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, achieving improvements of up to 2.5% in accuracy.

This study introduces a novel framework for predicting Alzheimer's disease cognitive phenotypes by integrating MRI-derived brain features with Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) scores. We employed a multimodal deep learning approach, where a 3D convolutional neural network extracts structural MRI features, while a separate linear model processes MMSE data; subsequently, a fusion network combines these outputs to generate predictions. We assessed the framework's efficacy across two distinct tasks: forecasting MMSE scores and predicting CDR-AD scores. Our method was benchmarked against a standard multimodal linear model and a single-modality structural MRI model. Furthermore, we examined the impact of varying the ratio of patients with mild cognitive impairment (MM) to Alzheimer's disease on the framework's performance. Results indicate that our proposed framework outperforms the single-modality structural MRI model in both prediction tasks. Additionally, the method demonstrates superior performance over the linear multimodal model, particularly in predicting CDR-AD scores.

This study examines the ethical analysis of artificial intelligence systems through the lens of argumentation theory, proposing a framework that integrates these two fields. By applying argumentation theory to AI Ethics literature, we identify that current practices often fail to adequately address the complexity of ethical analysis. Consequently, we introduce the concept of "ethical reasoning" as a vital component of AI Ethics and develop a novel method for representing such reasoning using structured arguments. Our approach involves creating a dedicated language and a corresponding formalism, along with defining an argumentation framework capable of detecting conflicts and contradictions. Finally, we present a formalism for ethical reasoning that incorporates this language and language-specific argumentation schemes, while also evaluating the strengths and limitations of our proposed method.

The paper investigates the decidability of properties concerning ω-words and finite automata, demonstrating that the class of Boolean-closed full trio families of ω-words is uniquely characterized as decidable. This result is derived by proving that a full trio of ω-words is a Boolean-closed trio if and only if it is a Boolean-closed triple, and by establishing that any family of finite subsets of ω-words that is closed under unions also remains a full trio when extended to ω-words. Additionally, we establish that finitely generated full trios are precisely those that are Boolean-closed, and we identify that finiteness constitutes the sole decidable Boolean-closed full trio for ω-words.

This study introduces a hybrid channel estimation framework designed for millimeter-wave (mmWave) systems, integrating a deep neural network (DNN) to enhance prediction accuracy. The approach begins by utilizing a DNN to forecast the sparsity vector of the channel, followed by applying least squares (LS) estimation to derive the complete channel based on that vector. Simulation outcomes demonstrate that this hybrid method outperforms traditional techniques, such as greedy algorithms, in terms of estimation accuracy.

Recent discrepancies between experimental results and Standard Model predictions for $V_{ud}$ and $V_{us}$ offer a compelling window into physics beyond the Standard Model. This paper examines the implications of these anomalies for the lepton sector, specifically the muon and electron. We demonstrate that a model featuring a light $Z^\prime$ boson can simultaneously resolve the $(g-2)_\mu$ anomaly along with the $V_{ud}$ and $V_{us}$ tensions. Furthermore, we explore the model's potential to account for the 3\alpha$ parameter tension, the $(g-2)_e$ discrepancy, and the anomalous electron magnetic moment.

This study introduces a new approach for 3D medical image segmentation that leverages dilated convolutional layers to capture extensive contextual details. By employing a dilated convolutional network, the proposed method effectively captures expansive receptive fields, thereby enhancing segmentation accuracy. Additionally, the work incorporates a dual-scale strategy that employs two convolutional networks with varying dilation rates to further boost performance. Experimental results on brain tumor segmentation using the BraTS 2018 dataset demonstrate that this dual-scale architecture outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques.

Data reuse and sharing are essential for advancing scientific research and innovation. However, when multiple data views are combined, there is a risk of exposing private data that conflicts with the shared information common to all views. This paper introduces a method to partition these views into separate sets: one containing shared data and another containing private data. Our approach begins by formulating the problem as a matrix completion task, where missing entries are estimated using a low-rank assumption. To achieve this, we develop a new algorithm called Multi-View Matrix Completion (MMC). Theoretically, we establish conditions for exact recovery and provide convergence guarantees. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed algorithm effectively minimizes data leakage while maintaining high accuracy in reconstructing shared data.

This study examines the correlation between the hot dust emission in galaxies and their radio emission, utilizing a sample of 100 nearby galaxies (z < 0.05) with available Spitzer/IRS spectra. We measured the flux density at 160 $\mu$m and the 160 $\mu$m/8 $\mu$m ratio for each galaxy. Our findings indicate that the hot dust emission is more intense in galaxies with higher radio luminosities and those exhibiting irregular morphologies. Furthermore, the hot dust luminosity correlates with the radio luminosity, a relationship that remains consistent across different morphological types. We also observed a strong link between the ratio of 160 $\mu$m/8 $\mu$m and the radio luminosity, which is independent of galaxy morphology. These results suggest that hot dust emission is a reliable tracer for radio emission in nearby galaxies.

Although recent advancements have propelled large language models toward human-level performance on various tasks, these systems often fall short in moral reasoning. This study introduces MORALCOT, a novel method for enhancing moral reasoning capabilities by leveraging the chain-of-thought technique. By prompting AI models to generate intermediate reasoning steps before reaching a conclusion, this approach not only boosts overall moral reasoning but also offers greater transparency in decision-making. We evaluated the method using the Moral Judgment Task (MJT), a standard benchmark for assessing moral development. Our findings reveal that generating intermediate reasoning steps significantly improves performance on the MJT, with the most notable gains observed in the two dilemmas that most severely challenge current language models.

The two-dimensional Dirac equation is fundamental to various domains, including condensed matter physics, graphene physics, and high-energy physics. This study introduces a novel numerical approach for solving this equation, utilizing the Crank-Nicholson scheme for temporal discretization and the spectral method for spatial handling. We demonstrate the method's stability and confirm convergence rates that align with theoretical predictions. Finally, several examples are presented to showcase the technique's efficacy.

Model Predictive Control (MPC) has proven highly effective for optimizing cooperative driving applications, such as platoon control, by leveraging the ability to forecast and mitigate the impact of interactions with surrounding vehicles. However, this approach is computationally demanding, often necessitating the solution of numerous optimization problems in real-time. To address this, we introduce a new method for constructing reduced-order models of MPC controllers by utilizing a graph-based representation of the problem's constraints. This representation facilitates the direct identification of inactive constraints, thereby shrinking the search space for the optimization solver. We further present a graph-based algorithm for aggregating multiple vehicles into a single reduced-order model. This algorithm is designed to be efficient, requiring only constant time relative to the number of vehicles involved. Finally, we demonstrate the method's efficacy through a case study involving a truck-tractor-trailer system.

The proliferation of social media has created a fertile environment for the dissemination of misinformation, which can cause significant harm to individuals and society. While the accuracy of content is often evaluated by examining the source, the validity of that source can be compromised if the source itself is biased. This study investigates whether users' perceptions of credibility are influenced by the number of endorsements a piece of information receives. We analyzed a dataset of 1.2 million tweets from Twitter, finding that the likelihood of users perceiving information as credible increases with the number of endorsements it accumulates. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the endorsement patterns of users are interconnected, suggesting that the networks of users who endorse specific content are more likely to resemble one another than occur by chance. These findings indicate that the social dynamics of online information sharing can shape how users judge the trustworthiness of content.

The integration of 5G and the Internet of Things (IoT) enables the creation of intelligent, self-organizing, and self-healing vehicular networks. This paper introduces $\pi$-ROAD, a $\pi$-calculus framework designed to facilitate the interconnection of IoT devices and 5G vehicles within smart transportation ecosystems. By leveraging $\pi$-calculus capabilities, the framework allows for the modeling of complex, dynamic, and heterogeneous environments, including scenarios involving road emergencies. The $\pi$-ROAD system is engineered to assist network operators in managing limited resources during crises, thereby enabling the rapid deployment of roadside units (RSUs) and the efficient distribution of emergency data to vehicles.

This study introduces a robot control framework designed to facilitate safe and efficient collaborative operations between a human and a robot. The system integrates a shared intention model, Artificial Potential Fields (APF) collision avoidance, and Model Predictive Control (MPC). Specifically, the shared intention model predicts the human's trajectory, while the APF algorithm generates repulsive forces to ensure the robot avoids the human and other obstacles. These calculations feed into the MPC controller, which optimizes the robot's path to minimize the distance from the human while adhering to safety constraints. The proposed framework was validated through a simulation of a shared workspace where a human and a mobile manipulator cooperatively assemble a part. Results indicate that the APF collision avoidance method introduces significant deviations in the robot's trajectory.

The trajectory of urban development is being driven by the convergence of heightened machine intelligence and increased levels of autonomy. This shift is fundamentally altering the built environment, transforming it into a vast ecosystem populated by numerous intelligent agents. These agents are increasingly capable of perceiving, reasoning, and acting within the city, thereby reshaping its social, economic, and physical landscapes. This paper examines the disruptive potential of these agents on the city's structure, analyzing their impact across the urban economy, social interactions, and the physical built environment.

This study investigates online caching with side information, where a cache of capacity $k$ receives requests over time. Before each request, the system predicts a side signal, which serves as an estimate of the optimal offline choice, aiming to retrieve. We introduce a novel online algorithm that leverages this predictive data to minimize the total number of misses. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that the algorithm's competitive ratio, relative to an optimal offline algorithm, is bounded by $O(\Delta + k)$, where $\Delta$ signifies the maximum prediction error and $k$ is the cache size. Furthermore, we introduce a specific online method for generating side information that achieves a competitive ratio of $O(\Delta + k)$ with a constant factor of $1/2$. Additionally, we present a randomized online caching strategy that attains an expected competitive ratio of $O(\Delta + k)$ with a constant factor of $1/3$.

This study introduces the Trilateral Attention Network (TrilNet), designed to enhance image segmentation by integrating a multi-path strategy. This approach leverages the distinct advantages inherent to different pathways, specifically: (1) a spatial pathway that delivers superior performance on standard datasets; (2) a spectral pathway that excels in handling noisy labels; and (3) a spatial-spectral combined pathway that achieves robust results across various data conditions. To address the challenge of selecting optimal paths for specific scenarios, we developed a dynamic fusion mechanism that integrates the TrilNet's multi-path strategy with a specialized pathway selection module. This module learns to identify the most effective pathway for a given input, thereby boosting segmentation accuracy. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that TrilNet surpasses current state-of-the-art methods, while the proposed fusion mechanism further improves performance by adapting to different contexts.

This paper examines the geometry of the linearized N=1, d=4 supersymmetric conformal field theory supermanifold. By imposing a set of torsion constraints on superspace, we derive the relationships between various gauge fields within linearized supergeometry. Furthermore, we establish framework for constructing a novel set of field strength supermultiplics derived from the commutation of the torsion-constrained covariant derivatives.

The efficacy of learning models relies heavily on the quality of their training data. While conventional methods evaluate this quality by analyzing the distribution of labels and features, we propose a complementary approach that assesses the specific impact of individual examples on model performance. By utilizing a novel metric, we determine the contribution of a single data point to a model's overall accuracy. We demonstrate that this metric effectively identifies examples that drive model quality, as well as those that hinder it. Furthermore, we illustrate how this approach can be leveraged to pinpoint specific data quality issues, such as labeling errors and data drift.

We examine how quantum anomalous Hall (QAH) states influence charge pumping within the two-dimensional (2D) quantum Hall surface. By analyzing the pumping current, we find that it arises from both a standard Abelian and a non-Abelian matrix Berry phase. The non-Abelian component, which is typically disregarded in current literature, is shown to be the dominant term. This contribution stems from the matrix-valued evolution of the many-body ground state, which is governed by the system's Hamiltonian. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the non-Abelian matrix Berry phase can be expressed as a geometric phase acting on the wavefunction of the system's edge states.

METRO-LM1 and METRO-LM2 are built upon the Qwen1.5-0.5 architecture, while METRO-LM3 utilizes the Qwen1.5-0.5 structure. We introduce a protocol for inferring the topology of a quantum network using solely local measurements. This approach is applicable to any network of quantum memory nodes linked via optical channels, regardless of the specific type of quantum links employed. The network's topology is reconstructed by analyzing the correlations between quantum memories at distinct nodes. Crucially, this inference process relies exclusively on locally accessible data: the states of quantum memories and the outcomes from Bell-state measurements executed at nodes. The proposed method is demonstrated using the Delft Quantum Internet testbed, successfully identifying the network's topology with 90% accuracy.

This research investigates how to present visualizations to individuals unfamiliar with the encodings used. We conducted a study comparing three distinct introduction strategies: (1) a direct explanation of visual elements, (2) a general description of the data, and (3) a detailed breakdown of the data. Results indicate that the general description strategy was the most effective, while visual explanations alone were the least helpful. Additionally, we observed that the most visually oriented encodings were the ones most beneficial when included in an introduction.

Optical manipulation of many-body systems has recently become a prominent area of research, promising to reveal the dynamics of quantum matter. However, rapid oscillations inherent to the driving field can cause Floquet heating, which may destroy long-range order. This work examines the interplay between Floquet heating and long-range order in the context of driving the one-dimensional transverse-field Ising model. We demonstrate that while the system's long-range order is generally suppressed by Floquet heating, specific parameter regimes can sustain long-range order even under drive. Furthermore, we show that these parameters can be precisely tuned to control the order's characteristics, such as the decay exponent of spin correlations.

Counterfactual reasoning is a powerful method for generating plans to achieve specific goals. This paper examines how uncertainty regarding model parameters affects the planning process. We introduce a novel approach to counterfactual planning that incorporates uncertainty regarding the environment's dynamics. Our method employs a Bayesian framework to iteratively refine the plan by updating the model with observations gathered during execution. We evaluate this approach in two settings: first, a simulated 2D gridworld, and second, a real-world robotic task involving a Baxter robot. Results indicate that our uncertainty-aware strategy produces more reliable counterfactual plans compared to methods that ignore such uncertainties.

This study introduces a novel, large-scale dataset designed for urban sound classification, featuring 1,000 distinct sound classes. The collection comprises 10,000 hours of audio gathered from 1,500 distinct locations across the United States, with a primary focus on enhancing dataset diversity and classification granularity. To address the challenge of limited labeled data, we propose a semi-supervised learning framework that leverages pseudo-labeling and data augmentation techniques. Experimental evaluations on both our new dataset and the established ESC-50 corpus demonstrate significant performance gains. Specifically, the model achieves 96.4% accuracy on ESC-50 and 51.3% accuracy on our new US8k test set. The source code and dataset are accessible at https://github.com/ashishbhatnagar/US-Data-and-Code.

This study examines the generalized Witten effect within the framework of quantum gravity, emphasizing its influence on the charged states' spectrum and its implications for black hole remnant structure. We demonstrate that the generalized Witten effect imposes a stringent constraint on black hole remnants, potentially eliminating the concept of the remnants themselves. Furthermore, we explore various quantum gravitational corrections arising from the generalized Witten effect and analyze their impact on black hole remnant structure.

This study examines the challenges of learning Nash equilibria in extensive two-player games, specifically focusing on the counterexample-guided (CEG) variant of \textit{regret pruning}. We demonstrate that the newly introduced variations of regret pruning proposed in [GKR20] are theoretically equivalent to the original approach by [GL12], albeit with a more streamlined proof. Furthermore, we introduce two enhancements to the CEG framework: first, we adapt the pruning procedure to prevent the unnecessary elimination of strategies that do not constitute rational moves; second, we integrate a technique for caching and reusing pruning outcomes across multiple queries. We validate these contributions through experiments on large-scale extensive-form games, revealing that the new regret pruning variants match the original method in effectiveness while the caching mechanism yields substantial additional gains.

This paper presents a novel modal logic designed to accommodate modal syllogistic theories regarding possible states-of-affairs. By doing so, it offers a fresh interpretation of Aristotle's modal syllogistic, a reading that had previously been suggested by Smith (1987) and Berto (2004). The study offers a comprehensive examination of the soundness and completeness of this system, alongside an investigation into its soundness and completeness relative to Smith's modal syllogistic framework.

Violating Bell inequalities serves as the standard method for certifying non-classicality in physical systems. In contrast, distinct "causal inequalities" are required to identify non-classicality within the causal structure of interactions. This study examines a streamlined extension of the standard Bell test designed to detect violations of such causal constraints. In classical scenarios, violating these causal inequalities demands significantly lower detection efficiencies than violating traditional Bell inequalities. However, quantum systems breach these causal inequalities with ease, even under conditions of imperfect detection. Consequently, a novel framework for certifying the non-classical nature of general physical processes is presented, wherein the observed statistics deviate from any combination of classical and quantum strategies.

This study introduces a dual-critic reinforcement learning framework designed to manage video encoding by jointly optimizing rate allocation and quantization. By employing two independent function approximators, the system manages both distortion and rate constraints. The dual-critic structure facilitates the resolution of the Lagrangian associated with this joint problem, thereby enabling an adaptive adjustment of the constraint's associated multiplier. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior compression efficiency compared to conventional techniques.

This study investigates the gas-phase chemistry of carbon and oxygen within protoplanetary disks, specifically examining how the photo-ablation of carbon-rich grains influences the chemical equilibrium cycle. We demonstrate that this ablation process sustains a long-lived equilibrium cycle, characterized by the formation of C$_2$H$_2$ and CO$_2$ from C, O, and CH, which is critical for understanding the gas-phase chemistry in these environments. Furthermore, we show that this ablation mechanism is essential for reproducing the observed abundance of C$_2$H$_2$ in the disk. Finally, we discuss the implications of these findings for the formation of carbon-rich planets.

This study introduces NeuralCut, a new approach for selecting cuts in mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) that leverages the strengths of both traditional methods and deep learning. By integrating a neural network with a specialized search mechanism, NeuralCraft identifies cut locations that surpass existing state-of-the-art baselines. Our experiments on the DIMACS 1992 and AIT 2010 benchmarks reveal that NeuralCut significantly outperforms current techniques, particularly on problems that are harder to solve.

The superconducting behavior of the topological superconductor candidate T$_d$-MoTe$_2$ was investigated by substituting Mo with Ir. This substitution induces a transition from an A-phase to a T$_d$-phase, resulting in a superconducting critical temperature ($T_c$) that rises from 0.2 K to 1.1 K. The superconducting gap in T$_d$-Mo$_{1-x}$Ir$_{x}$Te$_2$ is approximately 0.15 meV, which is significantly smaller than the 1.0 meV gap found in pure T$_d$-MoTe$_2$. Furthermore, the superconducting gap in the alloyed material exhibits a highly anisotropic, four-fold symmetric pattern, indicating that T$_d$-Mo$_{1-x}$Ir$_{x}$Te$_2$ displays s-wave superconductivity.

This study investigates the application of Natural Language Processing (NLP) methods to retrieve bug reports that are functionally identical, even if their textual descriptions differ. By analyzing the semantic relationships between bug descriptions and their linked code, we demonstrate that a combination of NLP techniques can significantly enhance search accuracy. Our proposed approach involves extracting code snippets associated with specific bug reports, converting them into word embeddings, and subsequently matching these embeddings against those of incoming reports to identify duplicates. Experimental results indicate that this method outperforms standard text-based similarity algorithms. Furthermore, we evaluate the impact of integrating different text-based and embedding-based similarity measures, confirming that the proposed technique effectively identifies functionally equivalent bugs.

We introduce an effective field theory that captures the essential characteristics of the anomalous Hall effect in graphene. This framework is highly strongly coupled, necessitating a perturbative approach. By employing the exact resummation of the leading logarithms, we establish a connection between the renormalized coupling constant and the phase transition.

This paper introduces a self-learning teacher-student framework designed to enhance Named Entity Recognition (NER) models. The teacher-student architecture is designed to iteratively refine the student's performance by leveraging both labeled and unlabeled data. The study evaluates the framework's effectiveness using a state-of-the-art BiLSTM-CRF model and investigates the impact of integrating various pre-trained word embeddings. The proposed method is assessed on the CoNLL-2003 and CoNLL-2003 datasets, with results indicating that the student model outperforms the original baseline.

The travel and hospitality sector is rapidly evolving, with social media platforms like Twitter becoming a primary resource for travelers seeking travel tips, reviews, and general advice. This study examines the nature of these tourism-related tweets to uncover novel insights that can enhance industry offerings. We introduce a novel approach that leverages Twitter's geolocation data to map the origins of tweets and identify key geographic hubs of tourism activity. By applying this technique to tweets concerning the United Kingdom, we discovered that while London remains the most active location, the volume of tweets from various regions has shifted over time. Furthermore, we conducted a detailed linguistic analysis of the tweet content, revealing that hotel recommendations are the most prevalent topic, followed by inquiries about transportation. These findings offer valuable guidance for businesses aiming to enhance their services and marketing strategies.

This study introduces a machine learning framework designed to forecast the effective properties of microstructured materials. The model utilizes a hybrid approach combining the graph neural network (GNN) architecture with the message-passing technique to process the geometric data of material structures. To train the model, a dataset comprising 1,000 samples was generated, each consisting of a 100-element structure with varying volume fractions. The resulting network successfully predicts macroscopic properties, including Young's modulus, Poisson's ratio, and the bulk and shear moduli, for unseen configurations. The model's performance was evaluated using mean absolute error (MAE) and root mean square error (RMSE) metrics. The findings demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior accuracy compared to existing state-of-the-art techniques.

We report the detection of a companion to the young star CI Tau at a separation of 0.14 arcseconds, corresponding to a projected distance of 20 au. Utilizing the 3.6-meter Canada-France-Hawaii Telescope, we employed the Gemini Planet Imager High-Contrast Imager (GPI-HC) to conduct this observation. The companion, designated CI Tau b, has a mass of 1.0 ± 0.1 Jupiter masses and a projected separation of 20 au. By combining this new detection with archival data from the Keck and Gemini observatories, we have established that the companion's migration has been minimal over the past 10 million years. Furthermore, angular differential imaging allows us to rule out companions with masses exceeding 0.01 Jupiter masses at separations less than 0.25 arcseconds, effectively eliminating the possibility of such low-mass objects causing the star's rotation.

We demonstrate that zero-energy trajectories of a specific potential correspond to finite-energy free-motion paths on a sphere, where the potential in question is defined as the generalized Calogero-Moser potential.

This paper examines the existence of non-trivial solutions for non-local integro-differential equations featuring an unbounded coefficient. These equations involve operators of order $s$ that are non-local and integro-differential in nature.

This study introduces a solution for unlabelled multi-object filtering that integrates the trajectory estimation benefits of Probabilistic Multi-Object Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) filters with the computational efficiency of Point Process filters. By utilizing a point process to represent the state of trajectories, the approach employs a point process-based proposal distribution to update these trajectories via Metropolis-Hastings updates within an MCMC framework. This integration retains the superior trajectory estimation capabilities of traditional MCMC filters while achieving significant computational gains comparable to point process filters. Additionally, the method is straightforward to implement, as it requires minimal modifications to existing multi-object filters that already utilize discrete particle representations for targets.

This paper introduces a novel stability assessment criterion for large power systems with high-penetration of power converters, utilizing a data-driven approach grounded in the theory of random dynamical systems. Unlike traditional methods that rely on linearized models, this approach leverages the system's inherent nonlinearity to evaluate stability under uncertain conditions. The framework defines stability based on the existence of a unique invariant measure and establishes sufficient conditions for its presence. Furthermore, the paper proposes a systematic method to identify the support of this measure, which represents the set of possible long-term system states. The applicability of this criterion is demonstrated through a case study on a 39-bus test system.

This study introduces a novel approach to signature verification that incorporates forgery detection, utilizing a deep neural network to generate signature templates. These templates are designed to maximize distinctiveness, complexity, and repeatability, thereby enhancing the system's ability to identify forged signs. The proposed method was evaluated against the public CASIA Signature Forgery Database, demonstrating performance that surpasses current state-of-the-art systems.

This work examines Hardy sums by interpreting them as oriented geodesics terminating at the boundary of hyperbolic space. We establish that these Hardy sums can be represented as specific integrations over sets defined by oriented geodesics.

Mobile applications have become a primary vehicle for delivering personalized experiences, yet they often struggle to gather sufficient context for accurate personalization. To address this, we propose a new method for persistently storing contextual values within the app environment. By maintaining a history of user interactions and associated contexts, these apps can effectively predict and tailor content to individual needs. We have developed a persistent context store (PStore) to facilitate this, which employs a learning model to infer user interests from stored context. Furthermore, we designed a user study to evaluate how well users perceive PStore's persistent context recommendations. The results indicate that participants found these recommendations both useful and engaging.

This paper introduces a novel real-time 6DoF pose estimation architecture that leverages a hybrid of convolutional and recurrent neural networks. By employing a recurrent structure, the system achieves superior accuracy compared to state-of-the-art methods relying solely on convolutional networks. Additionally, it delivers robust performance in challenging scenarios, such as when objects are partially occluded. The architecture's efficiency is further enhanced by a specialized input preprocessing technique that significantly reduces the input image size, enabling real-time processing speeds.

This study details the performance of AstroSat's Cadmium-Zinc-Telluride (CZT) imaging spectrometer, known as CZTS. The instrument operates in the 20–300 keV range and features a 128×128 pixel array with a 1.5 mm pitch, utilizing a 100 μm thick collimator to restrict its field of view to 1.5°×1.5°. The collimator is constructed from 10 mm thick lead with a 0.2 mm tungsten coating. The paper outlines the detector's specifications, calibration procedures, and performance metrics, alongside an analysis of the collimator's efficiency. The collimator's effectiveness is evaluated using the 300 keV Crab Nebula, while the imaging capabilities are verified through observations of the Crab, Cygnus X-1, and GX 339-4. Flux measurements for the Crab Nebula and Cygnus X-1 are deemed reliable, whereas data from GX 339-4 is considered preliminary. The study further presents the initial results of a survey targeting 100 selected sources from the 4π Swift/BAT catalog.

Blockchain protocols are categorized as either permissionless or permissioned based on the necessity of prior identity registration for participants. In permissioned systems, access requires pre-registration, whereas in permissionless networks, anyone can join anonymously. This paper examines the security protocols of both system types, specifically analyzing the implications of anonymity on system integrity. Furthermore, we introduce a formal framework for modeling these blockchain mechanisms and define a set of security properties that are independent of specific implementations. The discussion concludes with an analysis of Ethereum through the lens of our proposed formal model.

This study examines the mass spectra of the $X(3872)$ and $Z_c(3900)$ charmonium-like states using the improved chromomagnetic interaction (ICI) model. The model's parameters are calibrated based on the mass spectra of known $S$-wave and $D$-wave charmonium states. By applying this model, we calculate the masses of the $X(3872)$ and $Z_c(3900)$, finding that the $X(3872)$ is best described as a $D$-wave $c\bar{c}$ state, while the $Z_c(3872)$ is a $D$-wave $c\bar{c}$ state. This study examines the impact of the strong hypercolor interaction on the Higgs mass within a framework where the Standard Model is modified by a new strong SU(5) gauge interaction. We analyze how the magnitude of the strong coupling at the scale where the strong hypercolor force becomes non-perturbative influences the upper limits of the Higgs mass. Specifically, we demonstrate that these bounds are relaxed when the coupling at the instability scale is small, whereas they remain tight if the coupling at that same scale is large.

This study demonstrates that solutions to the Hamilton-Jacobi equation yield the $\mathsf{p}$-Talagrand inequality within Carnot groups. We additionally demonstrate that this inequality holds in spaces of homogeneous dimension $Q \geq 2$ when the $\mathsf{p}$-Laplacian features measurable coefficients. Furthermore, we establish that the $p$-Talagrand inequality is valid in Heisenberg groups for cases where the $\mathsf{p}$-Laplacian incorporates the Barenblatt term.

This paper introduces an exponentially weighted divergence (EWD) estimator for parametric regression, demonstrating its theoretical properties through asymptotic analysis. The proposed EWD estimator is shown to be more efficient than the density power divergence (DPD) estimator while offering greater robustness. Additionally, the study establishes asymptotic normality for the EWD estimator and validates its performance via a simulation analysis.

This study introduces a new method for segmenting moving objects in images. The approach begins by identifying pixels that are either static or dynamic, followed by a clustering process that groups these pixels based on their proximity. The resulting clusters are then evaluated to determine whether they represent static or moving elements. The proposed algorithm is validated against a set of standard test images, with performance compared to existing state-of-the-art techniques.

This paper investigates the link between periodic orbits on surfaces and the statistical characteristics of the characteristic polynomials of corresponding surface graphs. We demonstrate that coefficients in the characteristic polynomial are influenced by periodic orbits that self-intersect, and we establish a formula expressing these coefficients as zeta function derivatives, adjusted to account for self-intersections. Additionally, we derive an exact formula for the variance of coefficients within the family of surface graphs with genus $g$ by analyzing the space of homologically trivial, oriented, and undirected loops on a surface. Our findings indicate that the variance of coefficients in the zeta function of surface graphs is asymptotically lower than that observed in the case of random graphs.

This study introduces a new classification system for periodic variable stars, developed using a supervised machine learning approach. We utilized the Gaia Early Data Release 3 (GEDER3) to train a Random Forest model, employing light curve parameters (amplitude, period, and variability type) as input features. The model distinguishes between 10 specific classes of periodic variables, including eclipsing binaries and nebular variables, while also identifying outliers. We validated the trained classifier using a test set of 1,000 variables from the OGLE-IV catalog, achieving an accuracy of 96.5%. The classifier's performance is further evaluated on the GEDER3 catalog, where it successfully separates nebular variables from eclipsing binaries. Additionally, we demonstrate the utility of this tool by classifying 1,000 variables from the GEDER3 catalog, achieving an accuracy of 96.5%.

This study addresses the problem of characterizing the closest NEMI system to a given LTI network. By applying the concept of the closest NEMI system to a non-IM system, a unique solution is derived. Furthermore, the paper introduces a methodology for determining the closest NEMI system to a non-IM system, utilizing its inherent properties and the relationship between non-IM systems and their corresponding NIM counterparts.

Continual learning (CL) has recently gained significant attention in End-to-End Automatic Speech Recognition (EASR), enabling the incremental addition of new tasks to existing models without forgetting previously acquired knowledge. This paper investigates the application of CL to EASR, specifically examining the impact of task ordering and the influence of model scale. Our findings indicate that a top-performing CL approach can achieve results up to 10% lower word error rate (WER) on new tasks compared to standard fine-tuning, a gain that becomes even more pronounced with larger models. Furthermore, we demonstrate that a highly effective strategy for this EASR context involves utilizing a single model weight vector to represent all prior tasks.

Sentiment analysis is a vital component of social media analytics, yet it remains a significant challenge due to the prevalence of code-switching in social media messages. This paper introduces a code-switching detection model designed to identify code-switched segments within Indonesian tweets. The study utilizes a dataset comprising 1,000 manually annotated code-switching instances extracted from 1,000 tweets. The proposed approach employs a Transformer-based architecture enhanced with a multi-head attention mechanism. Experimental results demonstrate that the model achieves an F1-score of 0.71, surpassing the performance of both Bi-LSTM and Transformer models lacking multi-head attention.

This study examines the three-loop seesaw model, which generates Majorana neutrino masses through a combination of two distinct three-loop mechanisms. We analyze the phenomenology of this framework, focusing on lepton flavor violation and its potential detection at the LHC. Our results indicate that, within the parameter space allowing for realistic neutrino masses and mixings, the model predicts a charged scalar lighter than 129 GeV and a right-handed neutrino with mass below 100 GeV. These particles could be identified at the LHC through decays involving Higgs bosons or $Z$ bosons. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the model's predictions can be distinguished from those of the standard scenario, where right-handed neutrinos are the sole source of mass generation.

This study introduces a novel architecture for Product-based Neural Networks (PNNs) designed to capture interactions among categorical variables. The network's structure is engineered to model relationships between pairs of fields, with its capacity to learn these interactions dependent on the count of embedding layers employed. To enhance the model's ability to capture complex relationships, we propose a new embedding layer grounded in hypergraphs, which encodes interaction patterns across any number of fields. Experimental results indicate that this hypergraph-based approach outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in both tabular data classification and tabular data regression.

This study examines active transmitting beamforming design for a hybrid active transmitting beamforming (ATB) and intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) system, with the objective of maximizing the minimum rate of all users. The channel state information (CSI) for both the active transmit and IRS-assisted links is modeled as uncertain, with the uncertainty quantified via a statistical CSI error bound. The resulting optimization problem is non-convex due to the minimum-maximum rate formulation and the statistical CSI error constraint. To address this, we introduce a two-stage active transmit beamforming design. In the initial stage, we derive a closed-form solution for the active transmit beamforming vector by employing a weighted minimum variance distortionless response (WMDVR) filter. In the second stage, we determine the IRS phase shifts by applying the weighted minimum variance distortionless response (WMDVR) filter. The proposed approach is validated through numerical simulations, which demonstrate that accounting for channel state information uncertainty is essential for optimizing active transmitting beamforming in hybrid active transmitting beamforming and intelligent reflecting surface networks.

Branch prediction is a vital component of modern CPUs, and its accuracy is crucial for overall processor performance. While traditional fixed-bit predictors are common, dynamic approaches leveraging deep learning algorithms have recently emerged as a superior alternative. However, these deep learning models often struggle with generalization, leading to unstable predictions. To address this, we introduce a hybrid prediction mechanism that integrates a dynamic predictor with a static 2-bit predictor. This strategy significantly enhances stability and accuracy. Furthermore, we developed a novel, lightweight dynamic predictor based on a 3-layer Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) that outperforms comparable predictors. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed scheme surpasses state-of-the-art branch prediction accuracy.

This paper introduces a deep convolutional neural network designed to autonomously manage a camera's movements and positioning. The system tracks a target within a 3D environment, executing both pan and tilt adjustments to maintain continuous visual contact. By leveraging the network's ability to recognize objects and estimate their distance, the camera can navigate around obstacles and adjust its orientation to ensure optimal viewing angles. Experimental results indicate that this deep learning approach surpasses conventional PID control mechanisms in tracking accuracy and is capable of performing effectively in real-world scenarios.

This paper examines the Ising-SOS model on a high-dimensional half-space featuring a boundary field and an Ising-type action. By establishing non-normalisable boundary laws, we demonstrate the existence of a critical point, a phase transition, and a critical exponent. Furthermore, we prove that this model is equivalent to a specific representation of a spin system with a boundary magnetic field, a formulation previously established in the context of a spin system with a boundary field.

This study introduces a novel experimental approach to characterize entangled two-photon resonance energy transfer (E2P) within a single-molecule framework. By utilizing a single molecule of the fluorescent protein GFP, we measured the effective rate coefficient $K_{E2P}$, which serves as a metric for this specific energy transfer mechanism. The $K_{E2P}$ values were determined through a direct comparison of the fluorescence intensity of a solitary GFP molecule with that of a pair of molecules. The findings indicate that $K_{E2P}$ is governed by the distance between molecules, the relative orientation of their transition dipoles, and the spectral overlap between the fluorescence emission of the donor and the absorption cross-section of the acceptor. These results confirm the existence of a two-photon resonance energy transfer process that occurs between spatially separated, individually excited fluorescent chromophores.

This study examines the mass spectrum of the $B_c$ meson family by applying the light-cone QCD sum rule technique. The strong coupling constants associated with the transitions between $B_c$ mesons and their respective vector and axial-vector states are calculated using a similar method. Results indicate that these coupling strengths align well with predictions from QCD sum rules and lattice QCD. Furthermore, the mass spectrum of the $B_c$ system, along with its vector and axial-vector counterparts, is determined via light-cone QCD sum rules. The findings suggest that the mass predictions for these states are consistent with predictions made through perturbative QCD calculations.

This study examines the recent findings from the MicroBooNE collaboration, which have resolved the anomalous event excess previously reported by MINOS+ and MINOS. We investigate the potential of upcoming short-baseline neutrino oscillation experiments to address the longstanding tensions regarding sterile neutrinos, specifically the discrepancies between the MiniBooNE and MicroBooNE datasets, alongside anomalies in muon charge ratios and the LS37 data. Our analysis reveals that MicroBoNo's detection of neutral current interactions effectively rules out the interpretations of prior anomalies based on sterile neutrinos. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the predicted event rates for the Hyper-K experiment are sufficiently precise to detect the remaining sterile neutrino hints, thereby offering a definitive resolution to these anomalies.

This paper introduces a new approach to observational study design by leveraging the implicit sample weights generated by linear regression techniques. Drawing on these weights, we calculate the necessary sample sizes for a study designed to estimate causal effects. We demonstrate that this strategy yields optimal designs when the underlying data align with the model's assumptions, while offering a robust alternative when they do not. Theoretically, we establish that the method is robust to model misspecification and asymptotically efficient. We further illustrate its practical utility through a simulation study and a real-world application involving the estimation of the impact of early childhood education on test scores.

This study examines the impact of voltage source converters (VSCs) on grid dynamics. By modeling the VSC as a two-degree-of-freedom oscillator, we demonstrate that VSCs can mitigate oscillations in weakly interconnected grids. Furthermore, we explore the relationship between the damping of these controlled oscillations and the gain of the VSC control system. Finally, we address a critical challenge: when a weakly coupled grid contains multiple unstable modes, oscillation mitigation via VSCs may inadvertently trigger new oscillations or lead to a complete loss of stability.

We investigate the collective spontaneous emission of a single-mode light field generated by a cloud of stationary, two-level atoms. This process is modeled using the quantum Langevin formalism, which incorporates the atomic ensemble's collective dynamics and the associated quantum noise from a vacuum-coupled bosonic field. The resulting two-atom reduced density matrix is derived by tracing out the bosonic noise component. We demonstrate that emitted photons display strong quantum correlations, evidenced by a violation of a classical inequality, and we analyze the specific conditions under which this phenomenon occurs. Furthermore, we examine the non-Markovian characteristics of the system by calculating the quantum mutual information between the atomic ensemble and the bosonic noise.

This study examines the stability of kinks within a one-dimensional scalar field theory featuring internal modes. We establish that internal modes significantly influence kink stability, a finding that contradicts standard perturbation theory predictions. Furthermore, we introduce a novel theoretical framework designed to accurately model the impact of these internal modes on kink stability.

Generalized parton distributions (GPDs) are essential for understanding hadron-production mechanisms and high-energy scattering, as they connect to the $n$-th moments of these processes. This study examines the evolution of GPDs within the leading-order DGLAP framework, deriving a specific evolution kernel that incorporates the non-trivial color structure of quark-gluon mixing. Our findings indicate that the mixing contribution is substantial, necessitating its inclusion in any rigorous analysis of the DGLAP evolution.

Text classification is a prevalent natural language processing (NLP) task, where discrete data is mapped to specific categories. This paper introduces a straightforward yet effective method for text classification that leverages discrete noise. The core concept involves adding discrete noise to the input data, which effectively expands the model's decision boundaries. We demonstrate that this technique enhances performance across various datasets and architectures. Furthermore, we provide a theoretical analysis of the underlying principles and their impact.

Accurate polyp detection is essential for endoscopic procedures, yet the small size of polyps and the challenges posed by their diverse appearances and complex backgrounds make this task particularly difficult. To address these issues, we introduce a new channel-aware attention mechanism designed to aggregate video features more effectively. This approach leverages the temporal consistency inherent in endoscopy footage, where consecutive frames are highly correlated. By employing channel-specific attention, the method learns to prioritize specific channels that are most relevant to the current frame, thereby enhancing feature aggregation. Experimental results demonstrate that this mechanism surpasses existing state-of-the-art techniques in both accuracy and efficiency. Furthermore, the method is flexible enough to be integrated with various existing video models, allowing for a significant boost in performance.

This work introduces a sequential sampling technique that allows for the regulation of spreading intensity and can be adapted to various data structures, including those with missing values. The method is grounded in a Bayesian framework, where the spread magnitude is governed by a specific parameter. To facilitate efficient sequential sampling, the authors propose a novel approach to approximate the posterior distribution. The study outlines the algorithm's implementation and details how the spreading intensity can be controlled. Furthermore, a simulation study is conducted to evaluate the performance of the proposed method.

The rp-process is a rapid proton-capture sequence occurring in Type-I X-ray bursts, where the reaction flow is governed by the interplay between nuclear reaction rates and the $\beta$-decay lifetimes of unstable nuclei. This study examines the impact of $\beta$-decay rates on the reaction path, utilizing experimental data from the NSCL facility to measure lifetimes for key isotopes: $^{56}$Ni, $^{60}$Se, $^{64}$Se, and $^{68}$Se. The results indicate that approximately 60% of the reaction flow bypasses the waiting point $^{56}$Ni, with an additional 30% of the flow circumventing the waiting point $^{60}$Se.

This work extends Drinfeld's description regarding the irreducible components of the basic locus in ordinary abelian schemes to the broader context of ordinary abelian schemes equipped with a finite flat group scheme action. Specifically, we demonstrate that the flat part of the special fiber of the relative Cartier–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–Lust–

The recent Very High Energy (HEV) gamma-ray observations from the Fermi-LAT have significantly refined our understanding of the Milky Way's gamma-ray sources. This study utilizes the HEV gamma-ray fluxes from 140 known sources to refine the parameters of the gamma-ray model. The analysis employs a Bayesian framework to derive the posterior probability distributions for the model's hyperparameters, subsequently calculating the 68% credible intervals for the spatial distribution of the diffuse gamma-ray emission.

This work examines a diffusion model within a bounded domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ subject to nonlocal boundary conditions. Specifically, the flux across the boundary $\partial \Omega$ is determined by an integral over the entire domain, incorporating a kernel $K(x,y)$ that encodes the domain's geometric properties. The analysis focuses on the existence and uniqueness of the solution to the associated initial-boundary value problem, as well as the asymptotic behavior of solutions as $t \to \infty$.

This study introduces a machine learning approach to classify compact stellar systems (CSSs) into two categories: globular clusters (GCs) and dwarf galaxies (DGs). Utilizing the Gaia-ESO Survey (GES) database, we analyzed 1,000 CSSs, focusing on 600 objects with complete datasets containing 14 GES chemical elements. We employed a Random Forest (RF) classifier to determine the optimal set of features for distinguishing GCs from DGs. Our results indicate that the [Fe/H] abundance, along with the [Mg/Fe] and [Al/Fe] ratios, are the most critical indicators for classification. Furthermore, we identified that [Mg/Fe] and [Al/Fe] serve as the most effective features for separating GCs from DGs. The model's performance was evaluated using a 10-fold cross-validation method, achieving an overall accuracy of 89.5%. Additionally, we examined the impact of the number of training samples on the model's accuracy.

Simulations are a potent instrument for the construction of Recommender Systems, capable of modeling diverse scenarios to evaluate system performance and explore various configurations. This paper introduces a simulation framework for Recommender Systems, detailing its implementation and demonstrating its application.

This paper introduces a hypothesis testing framework applicable to distributions characterized by infinite mean or variance. The approach utilizes truncated sample means to estimate parameters and determine test statistics. The text establishes the asymptotic properties of the resulting test statistics and provides simulation results that demonstrate the method's performance.

The rise of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) has significantly advanced Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) research, yet CNNs face two primary limitations when processing EEG data: first, they are designed for grid-based inputs like images, whereas EEG signals are time-series data; second, CNNs typically discard temporal information by reducing data dimensions via pooling layers. To address these issues, this study introduces a new architecture called the Recurrent Convolutional Neural Network (RCNN) specifically for BCI applications. The proposed RCNN integrates the strengths of both CNNs and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) to effectively model both spatial and temporal characteristics of EEG signals. Experimental results demonstrate that RCNN outperforms existing methods, achieving an average accuracy of 91.1% on the BCI Competition IV dataset II.

This study investigates the $AdS/CFT$ correspondence for a massive scalar field within a noncommutative space, employing the Moyal-Deformed Dirac Neumann Boundary Condition (MDNBC). We derive the $AdS/CFT$ relation for a massive scalar field placed in a noncommutative bulk and analyze the resulting two-point correlation function of the dual CFT. By examining the behavior of this correlation function, we demonstrate that noncommutativity influences the properties of the dual field theory.

This study examines the optimal acceptance of kidney transplants for patients awaiting them, utilizing a Markov Decision Process (MDP) framework that accounts for patient mortality, waiting list clearance, and graft incompatibility. The authors propose a novel MDP model that incorporates incompatibility as a state variable, thereby enabling the assessment of specific transplant decisions. The authors also present an algorithm designed to calculate the optimal policy for this enhanced model. The efficacy of this algorithm is demonstrated through numerical examples, which further illustrate the significance of integrating incompatibility into the MDP framework.

This study examines the geometric characteristics of Hidden Markow Model (HMM) latent spaces, which are frequently utilized in natural language processing. We demonstrate that these HMM latent spaces are inherently discrete, possessing structural similarities to Hidden Layer Networks (LSMs) that are capable of representing discrete data. Furthermore, we establish that the Long Short-Term Memory Model's hidden states can be reduced to a space with finite dimensions.

This study examines weighted Bergman spaces $A^2(\mathbb{B}^n, v)$ and $H^\infty(\mathbb{B}^n, v)$, where $\mathbb{B}^n$ represents the unit ball in $\mathbb{C}^n$ and $v$ is a radial weight function. We provide characterizations for compact, power-compact, and Schatten class membership of operators on these spaces, as well as characterize the ideal within the space consisting of operators that belong to both weighted Bergman spaces.

Compressed architectures offer a promising method to reduce the substantial computational costs associated with training and deploying large language models. This study evaluates various compression strategies, including quantization, sparsification, and their hybrid approaches, specifically for text classification. We assess these techniques across three distinct datasets: the IMDB movie review sentiment dataset, the AG's News topic classification dataset, and the WikiQA dataset. Our findings indicate that while various compressed models perform adequately, a BERT-Large architecture with mixed precision quantization delivers the optimal balance between compression efficiency and performance.

The field of high-energy physics is currently undergoing a profound transformation, primarily driven by the escalating scale of data collection and analysis. This trend is expected to intensify in the near future, compelling the community to adopt a new professional role: that of a Data Scientist. This article outlines the essential competencies required for this emerging role, alongside an examination of how high-energy physics can leverage the expertise of established data science professionals.

We define a generalized concept of Howe curves and establish a correspondence between decomposed Richelot isogenies and these curves. Furthermore, we examine specific properties of generalized Howe curves and utilize them to construct a lift in the formal Lie ring of the Jacobian of a curve to a torus via a decomposed Richelot path.

This work introduces a methodology for analyzing errors in approximating a given matrix $A$ by a matrix drawn from a probability distribution $\mu$ defined on a compact and convex support set $\mathcal{S}$, where $\mu$ is supported by the invariant matrix theory. The theory establishes that there exists a unique probability measure supported on $\mathcal{S}$ that yields the maximal mean eigenvalues for any matrix $M$ sampled from $\mu$. This measure is termed the invariant measure. The proposed approach leverages this concept to deliver precise error assessments for both individual matrix instances and their expectations. Furthermore, it is demonstrated that for a broad class of support sets, the invariant measure can be explicitly determined.

This study examines the distribution of hyperlinks within Wikipedia articles, comparing raw wikitext against rendered HTML. We analyze the total link count, the frequency of each link's text, and the target domains. Our findings indicate that raw wikitext contains significantly fewer internal and external links than HTML versions. Furthermore, we observe that link text is often truncated in raw wikitext and that rendered links tend to direct toward a broader range of external domains. Additionally, we evaluate the security implications of rendering wikitext by identifying potentially harmful external websites referenced in articles.

We introduce a novel method for creating polar domains within twisted bilayers, which exhibit distinct twisted boundary conditions. These boundary conditions facilitate the application of a polar vector to these domains, thereby establishing a new dimension in twisted bilayer space. This development significantly expands the possibilities for twisted bilayers in topological physics.

This study examines the movement of light within a static, spherically symmetric, non-flat universe. By employing a geometric optics approach, we derive the photon trajectories and analyze how the spacetime's geometry influences these paths. Our findings indicate that, regarding the qualitative behavior of light propagation, the specific curvature of the spacetime does not alter the outcomes; these outcomes match those of flat universe models.

This study investigates the behavior of an alternating hill-and-valley wavy wall within a liquid crystal medium. We examine how these geometric features influence a trajectory of a single colloidal particle, specifically analyzing the effects of a potential energy landscape on its motion. The colloidal particle is modeled as a Brownian particle subject to a potential force, and its movement is simulated using Langevin dynamics. We demonstrate that the colloidal path is significantly altered by the specific parameters of the potential, such as the height of hills and the depth of wells. Furthermore, we analyze the relationship between the colloidal particle's trajectory and the potential energy landscape, revealing that the particle's motion is highly sensitive to these underlying structural variations.

The Roche limit defines the minimum distance at which tidal forces can disrupt a celestial body. While this limit is often used to explain the formation of small, irregularly shaped asteroids, it is not the sole mechanism responsible for their irregularity. This study investigates how elongation changes relative to the Roche limit to determine asteroid sensitivity to tidal effects. Using a sample of 10,000 main-belt asteroids, we calculated elongation based on the Roche limit and compared these values to those of small, near-Earth asteroids (NEAs) and comets. Our results indicate that elongation increases with proximity to the Roche limit, regardless of whether the object is an asteroid, comet, or NEA. This finding suggests that these objects may be sensitive to tidal forces beyond the Roche limit. Furthermore, elongation correlates with the object's size, implying that smaller bodies are more susceptible to tidal effects. We propose that tidal effects may have contributed to the formation of the small, irregularly shaped asteroids found in the inner solar system.

This study introduces a hybrid framework combining machine learning (ML) and quantum computing (QC) to investigate rare conformational transitions in molecular dynamics simulations. The approach employs quantum-inspired algorithms to generate ML potentials, which are then utilized to simulate molecular dynamics. The efficacy of this method is demonstrated through a case study on the folding of a 20-residue protein, where the quantum-assisted ML (QAML) approach successfully captures folding pathways and kinetics comparable to those derived from classical neural networks. Additionally, we examine the potential advantages of quantum computing in accelerating these ML-informed molecular dynamics workflows.

The newly created Monte-Carlo code MAPPIES (Modelling And Polarisation Prediction Inverse Engineered Source) is designed to forecast polarisation characteristics in X-ray and gamma-ray emissions resulting from the Compton scattering of photons by free electrons. This tool facilitates the investigation of polarisation phenomena in astrophysical sources, particularly those with complex geometries. The code's efficacy is validated through comparisons with experimental data from synchrotron facilities, specifically the Advanced Photon Source and the European XFEL. Additionally, it is applied to analyze the polarization properties of the Cygnus X-1 system, a notable X-ray binary.

This study examines how the seasonal progression of categories in sea-ice thickness evolves in relation to the expansion of open water areas within the Arctic. Utilizing the CICE model, we simulated a scenario where open water is absent, contrasting it with a realistic configuration featuring open water. The analysis focuses on the seasonal changes of these thickness categories in the Eureka region. The findings indicate that omitting open water leads to an overestimation of the total number of categories in sea-ice thickness evolution.

This paper presents a family of Hermitian curve-based curves, denoted as $\mathcal{X}_{a,b,n,s}$ and $\mathcal{Y}_{n,s}$, which exhibit specific arithmetic and geometric properties. The curves $\mathcal{X}_{a,b,n,s}$ represent a composite of two distinct coverings over a Hermitian curve, whereas $\mathcal{Y}_{n,s}$ forms an abelian cover of the same. We establish an explicit formula for the number of rational points on both families, which is then utilized to derive several new examples of curves possessing exceptional asymptotic behavior for the function $a_{g}(n)$.

Despite the recent emergence of high-quality singing voice synthesis techniques, significant hurdles persist for both academic and commercial applications. This paper introduces a novel dataset comprising 1,000 songs, each with 16 tracks of isolated instrumentals, totaling 16 tracks per song, and 1,000 songs, each with 1,000 songs, each with 1,000 songs, each with 1,000 songs, each with 1,000 songs, each with 1,000 songs, each with 1,000 songs, each with 1,000 songs, each with 1,000 songs, each with 1,000 songs, each with 1,000 songs, each with 1,000 songs, each with 1,000 songs, each with 1,000 songs, each with 1,000 songs, each with 1,000 songs, each with 1,000 songs, each with 1,000 songs, each with 1,000 songs, each with 1,000 songs, each with 1,000 songs, each with 1,000 songs, each with 1,000 songs, each with 1,000 songs, each with 1,

This paper introduces NIPS4Bplus, an enhanced version of the NIPS dataset, which features extended audio recordings from the same sites. Originally created to assess the performance of bird species classifiers, the dataset has been adapted to explore the potential of NIPS audio data for ecoacoustic research and the monitoring of avian populations. The authors present a comprehensive analysis of the dataset's characteristics, evaluate the impact of extended recording durations, and demonstrate a baseline approach for bird population monitoring utilizing this data.

This paper introduces a unified framework for event and frame camera calibration. Our method leverages a single static scene to determine intrinsic parameters for event and frame cameras, as well as their extrinsic transformation matrix, effectively addressing the fundamental challenge of aligning these disparate sensor types. Specifically, extrinsic calibration with our approach is feasible even when the frame camera lacks precise calibration. The event-to-frame model supports a wide range of calibration patterns, enabling flexible and versatile usage. Furthermore, the framework is adaptable to various frame camera types, including those with rolling and global shutters. Extensive experiments validate the efficacy of our method.

Graph learning has proven effective in numerous domains, including social networking, e-commerce, knowledge graphs, and biological networks. However, the specific data distribution and structural characteristics of these applications vary significantly. To address this, we introduce a unified graph learning framework capable of handling diverse graph types. Our approach utilizes a graph neural network (GNN) to generate node embeddings, which are subsequently refined by a variational autoencoder (VAE) to produce final representations. The GNN component is trained using a contrastive learning strategy, while the VAE component is optimized via a reconstruction loss function. We demonstrate the efficacy of this framework across multiple graph scenarios, such as homophilic and heterophilic social networks, e-commerce networks, and biological networks. Experimental results confirm that our model outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in node classification tasks.

This paper demonstrates that the braid group acting on four strands within the birshehnhout surface of degree 2 ($F_2$) arises from an exceptional collection. We also prove that the cluster group of $F_2$ functions as a quotient of the four-strand braid group. Additionally, we establish a homomorphism mapping the cluster group of the conifold singularity to the braid group of $\mathbb{P}^2$, alongside an isomorphism between the cluster group of the conifold and the cluster group of the affine A1 singularity.

This study introduces a 3D guidance system for retinal surgery, utilizing a projector to illuminate the retina and a camera to capture images. By monitoring the projected spot's position, the system provides real-time navigation for the surgeon. A key advantage is that the projector's light serves a dual purpose: it illuminates the retina and acts as a tracking marker, thereby eliminating the need for separate illumination sources or markers. Furthermore, the projector's light beam is visible to the camera, enabling direct 3D guidance without external fiducial markers. The system's accuracy was validated through experiments using a 3D printed model of an eye, demonstrating a mean absolute error of 0.63 mm and a 95% confidence interval of 1.13 mm.

This paper expands the product formula associated with $F$-polynomials for cluster algebras of type $A$ into a specific summation of products. This expansion is grounded in the product formula originally formulated by Fock and Goncharov, alongside an expansion of the exchange polynomials found in a work by Fomin and Zelevinsky.

The FIDO2 standard is driving the adoption of passwordless authentication, yet its current implementation relies on HTTPS, which introduces latency and security risks. This paper introduces FIDO2-QUIC, a framework that enables secure, low-latency FIDO2 authentication using the QUIC protocol. We detail the architectural design of FIDO2-QUIC, along with a proof-of-concept implementation and evaluation. Our findings demonstrate that FIDO2-QUIC significantly outperforms the traditional HTTPS-based approach in terms of both latency and security.

We demonstrate that a novel Weyl-Wigner approach fails to capture fundamental aspects of qubit quantum mechanics. In this framework, qubit states are represented by rays in a four-dimensional real vector space, with the Weyl-Wigner transform applied to real-valued functions within that space. The corresponding phase space is constructed using the Pauli matrices. Our analysis indicates that this approach struggles to model interference effects and entanglement. The resulting phase space is isomorphic to the standard Bloch sphere, yet we argue that this mapping inadequately reflects the specific geometry of the state space.

This paper introduces a novel video interface that integrates a dynamic, interactive visual summary, offering users enhanced autonomy and a sense of agency. By enabling viewers to adjust the playback speed of a scene, the system allows them to navigate content at a pace that suits their specific needs. We present a comprehensive evaluation of this approach, contrasting it with traditional interfaces. Our findings indicate that this innovative interface is not only more intuitive but also elicits a heightened sense of control.

This work examines the expressive power of the $\pi$-calculus against that of reactive Turing machines (RTTMs), focusing on behaviors that cannot be executed finitely. The study demonstrates that within the realm of finite-memory behaviors, the $\pi$-calculus is strictly more expressive than the RTTMs. Furthermore, it establishes a theoretical equivalence between the two frameworks, proving that any reactive Turing machine can be faithfully represented by an equivalent $\pi$-process.

This study presents a designed Gray code for ordered trees, where each successive representation is created by adding a leaf to the previous one. This specific code is constructed using a depth-first search algorithm.

This study introduces a novel deep learning framework designed to reconstruct particle tracks in heavy-ion collisions, utilizing a specialized neural network to identify and reconstruct charged particle trajectories. Addressing the challenges of track finding in such environments—specifically the high track density and significant multiple scattering effects—this approach leverages the network's capacity to model complex, non-linear relationships between tracks and their underlying data. The method is evaluated against standard algorithms using simulated data from the ALICE experiment at the LHC. Results indicate that the proposed deep learning technique surpasses the performance of the standard Sequential Kalman Filter (SKF) and the Generalized Kalman Filter (GKF) in terms of tracking efficiency.

The time-discontinuous prismatic space-time (D-PST) approach is a novel method designed to address the persistent difficulties in applying the finite-element method to finite-depth, free-surface simulations. By utilizing a distinct space-time element for each time step, D-PST overcomes the need for space-time continuity, thereby eliminating issues with hanging elements and complex mesh partitioning. The element's prismatic geometry allows for a flexible, unstructured grid that adapts to changing spatial domains over time. This flexibility enables the use of highly non-uniform grids, which are particularly advantageous for capturing sharp gradients and wave fronts. The method's accuracy is validated through numerical experiments involving solitary waves, demonstrating its effectiveness in free-surface flow modeling.
